Knowing the likely outcome cut turnout by about 11 points in a French natural experiment, and win probabilities make a race look more decided than vote shares do (US). Anger at specific failures mobilises (US). In a 61-million-user US experiment the effect passed on through close friends exceeded the direct effect.
audiences.message: Nothing is decided. People like you are voting. What is at stake is a commission, a fair draft and the next four years. Make your plan, and remind three friends to vote.
audiences.messenger: All four leaders to their own voters, then family, friends and local volunteers.
audiences.channel: Supporters' own WhatsApp and Telegram groups, friend-to-friend messages, earned news, the allocated broadcasts, and the field programme in positive-value stations (see Field).
audiences.avoid: Public victory talk, which wakes Likud's base. Panic messages. Win probabilities: talk in seats and votes. Leaking internal polls, which counts as publishing a poll during the blackout. Attacks on allied lists. Shareable content that mocks other communities: posts about the out-group are shared about twice as often and draw angry reactions (US).

audiences.size_note: The atlas's Druze and Circassian segment has about 96,000 eligible voters in 18 localities, with 2022 turnout of about 49%. Zionist parties won about 90% of the vote in Druze towns in 2022. Druze turnout fell from about 80% in 1996 and 1999 to about 50% in 2021 and 2022. The atlas holds Druze towns out of its budgets until a check of the filed CEC lists and a Druze poll, and does not target the Golan Druze villages.
audiences.what_moves: Druze voting is mainly utilitarian and candidate-led: support goes to parties expected to govern or with a local or family candidate. Kinship and Druze candidates on the list were the strongest predictors in a 2003-2022 study, and parties with a Druze candidate in a winnable slot have usually won the most votes in that candidate's home village. The grievances are Kaminitz-law fines and demolitions, the planning and housing shortage, and the Nation-State Law. One expert suggested Israel's 2025 moves to protect Druze in Syria could shift votes toward Netanyahu (expert view, no polling).
audiences.message: Equal partnership for those who serve together: planning and zoning relief, an answer on fines and demolitions, and equality under the law. Only commitments that are in the lists' published platforms or cleared by list leadership.
audiences.messenger: Druze candidates on the change lists and local Druze leaders, such as Yashar's Kamil Abu Rokon, a retired general (his list slot was not verified). Never outside spokespeople speaking for the community.
audiences.channel: Candidate-led house meetings, local WhatsApp networks, and the Hebrew and Arabic local media the candidates choose.
audiences.avoid: Calling Druze towns 'change-majority'. Treating Druze voters as one bloc. Promises not in platforms. Any activity in the Golan Druze villages. Headline targets before the candidate check. Change-list Druze candidates attacking each other.

audiences.size_note: Arab and Druze turnout was 53.2% in 2022, and Jewish parties won 14.3% of Arab votes. Ra'am's leader puts Arab support for Zionist parties this year at no more than 10-12%. The atlas publishes no town-level values for Arab localities and plans nothing there. Arab-sector turnout is a leadership decision, not a messaging one.
audiences.what_moves: Crime and personal safety dominate: 53.5% of Arab respondents put crime in their top two issues (IDI, Aug-Sep), and more than 140 people were killed in Arab communities by late June. Young Arab citizens want concrete plans on crime, housing, jobs and discrimination rather than general talk of partnership. 77% of Arab respondents supported an Arab party joining the next coalition (May). The Supreme Court unanimously overturned the CEC's disqualification of the Joint List and Ra'am on 2 Oct. The Task Force on Arab Citizens warns that framing reliance on Arab parties as illegitimate deepens alienation.
audiences.message: Equal citizenship and personal safety for every citizen, a serious national plan against crime, and respect in how the bloc speaks about Arab citizens. The same message in Hebrew and in Arabic.
audiences.messenger: Each list's own Arab and Druze candidates in their own campaigns, such as the Democrats' Arabic outreach. The bloc does not script messages for Arab lists or civil-society groups.
audiences.channel: The lists' own Arabic-language pages, interviews in Arabic media, and national broadcasts that speak to all citizens.
audiences.avoid: Any change-bloc-run or branded turnout activity among Arab voters, and any turnout targeting of Arab towns or of stations where Arab lists lead. Rides or anything of value. Delegitimising language. Saying different things in Hebrew and Arabic. Any support for Arab-sector turnout is a leadership decision, independent, transparent and cleared by election counsel.

media.channel: TV and radio: allocated election broadcasts (paid spots are banned)
media.role: The bloc's only campaign airtime on TV and radio. Use it to teach ballot letters, keep the bloc's issues on the agenda and close on turnout. Put the best tested spots late.
media.evidence: TV ads move vote intention a little and briefly. In 59 US experiments the average effect on vote choice was about 0.7 points and not significant. In a randomised Texas test a large TV buy had strong effects that had nearly vanished within about a week, and about half the ad effect that survived to a US election day came from the final week. Broadcast ads in neighbouring US counties changed who voted rather than how many voted. Cheap ads did not raise candidates' name recognition. All of this evidence is foreign.
media.rules: Radio and TV propaganda is banned for 60 days before the vote except the allocated broadcasts, which run 13-26 Oct, with no TV slots on statutory rest days. Each list gets 7 TV and 15 radio minutes, plus 2 TV and 4 radio minutes per MK of its outgoing faction, so a list built on a 24-MK faction gets 55 TV minutes and a list with none gets 7. TV content is approved by the CEC chair. Broadcast propaganda ends at 19:00 on Mon 26 Oct. No IDF framing, and written consent for images of the fallen, the wounded or victims. No poll figures after Fri 23 Oct.

media.channel: Paid digital and social ads (Meta, Google, YouTube)
media.role: Persuasion with tested creative in the final days, threshold-insurance messages for Blue and White voters, and volunteer recruitment. Not a turnout tool.
media.evidence: In the largest field test, an $8.9 million, eight-month Facebook and Instagram programme aimed at about 2 million US persuadable voters had no average effect on turnout. Party-brand ads randomised by ZIP code moved Democratic vote share by -0.04 points (SE 0.85) in Florida. In the closest analogue, a CDU campaign in the 2016 Berlin multiparty election, the sponsor gained 0.7 points (not significant), the opposing camp fell 1.4 points and same-camp parties also gained. Ads did not raise name recognition. In US campaigns' own tests ad effects vary about 50% around the average. In US survey experiments, pretest-based machine-learning targeting beat a single best message by about 70% on policy views, mostly on one issue, with no gain from using more than one trait. Persuasion fades with a half-life of days. All of this evidence is foreign.
media.rules: Every ad, including paid content, names who ordered it and how to contact them. Synthetic or altered content carries the CEC deepfake label for its full length. Political ads on Meta and Google are public in ad libraries with run dates and spend, so assume Likud and journalists read the bloc's ads. No poll figures from Sat 24 Oct.

media.role: The bloc's main channel for turnout and rapid response. Supporters forward short, tested audio and video to their own family and community groups, and personally ask friends to vote.
media.evidence: In 2024, 65% of Jewish Israelis got news via WhatsApp and 44% via Telegram, and family and friends' groups were trusted by more than 60% against 39-47% for groups run by politicians or journalists. In a 61-million-user US Facebook experiment the effect passed to close friends exceeded the direct effect. In India's Tamil Nadu, party WhatsApp groups moved moderate voters toward the party, mainly through members' own posts, without raising hostility. People reshare debunks from close or like-minded contacts, and audio works best (India and Pakistan). Friend-to-friend texting raised turnout about 2-3 points among those assigned (US). Israeli WhatsApp discussion grew less polarised over time, unlike Twitter. Likud ran its campaign largely through WhatsApp groups and a Telegram chatbot for about three years.
media.rules: Messages from a list segmented by a personal trait count as direct mail under privacy law and need a notice, the database controller, the data source and an opt-out. Volunteers writing to their own contacts is the lower-risk format. WhatsApp bans accounts for bulk or automated sending, and one wrongful block can stall an operation, so spread sending across real volunteer accounts and avoid automation in the final days. No lists of who has not voted. No voter-level data passes between lists without written counsel clearance.

media.channel: Earned media and news (Channel 12/N12, ynet, Kan, Channel 13)
media.role: Set the agenda on the bloc's issues and let leaders claim issue ownership in interviews and news events timed for the evening news.
media.evidence: In 2024 Channel 12 was the main news source for 51% of Jewish Israelis, ynet the main online source for 40%, and Kan the most trusted outlet. Channel 14 was watched by 24% of the right and about 4% of the centre. On one April 2026 night Channel 12's evening news drew about 411,000 viewers, about twice Channel 14's. Across four Israeli elections, TV coverage drove which issue people named as the top problem. A news-style exposure shifted issue ownership in a Belgian experiment, most on issues no party owned. Israel Hayom moved votes to the right through persuasion, about 0.22 points of right-bloc share per point of local exposure in 2013, so the Netanyahu bloc's own media are a structural asset two weeks of spending cannot match.
media.rules: No IDF framing in campaign material. Edited clips need an archived source file: Likud has petitioned against three Yashar videos for misleading editing. Use X to brief journalists, not to persuade. Any poll the bloc releases carries the full disclosure, and none after Fri 23 Oct.

media.role: Yisrael Beytenu's main channel to Russian speakers, plus Russian versions of the bloc's core content and a how-to-vote card.
media.evidence: In a self-selected reader poll of NEWSru.co.il (n=2,981, January 2024, low confidence), news sites were the main source (87%), Channel 9 was the most-watched TV channel (38%), Facebook (61%) and Telegram (47%) led social media, and use of Russian-language Telegram for war news rose from 18% to 40%. Russian speakers are about 15% of the population. Invalid ballots ran higher in Russian-speaking-segment localities (0.80%) than in liberal cities (0.35%) in 2022.
media.rules: The same law as Hebrew content: the 'ordered by' line, deepfake labels and the poll ban. Monitor Russian-language Telegram for misinformation, since the state has no national system to catch it.

media.role: Each list's own campaign in Arabic and the bloc's national message to all citizens, said the same way in both languages. Not a turnout channel.
media.evidence: Arab adults use TikTok (71%, 58% daily) and Telegram (66%, 28% daily). Arab respondents rank crime first. The Democrats are expanding Arabic social media and touring Arab towns. No verified data on the reach of Arabic-language outlets was found.
media.rules: No change-bloc-run or branded turnout content, and no turnout targeting of Arab towns or of stations where Arab lists lead. Any support for Arab-sector turnout is a leadership decision, independent, transparent and cleared by election counsel. Monitor Arabic networks for misinformation about the bloc.

media.role: News-cycle events, not vote movers. Accept on terms that suit the leader, and prepare for the security-incident and Arab-party questions.
media.evidence: Across 62 elections in 10 countries, TV debates had no detectable effect on vote choice. A leader's news performance can shift issue ownership (Belgian experiment). In a multi-candidate race the attacker lost and the bystander gained (Italy). No information on a 2026 debate was verified.
media.rules: No attacks on allied leaders on stage. No IDF props or framing. Answer the Arab-party question only with the agreed joint line.

media.role: Reach young voters on Instagram and TikTok, and give soft-right and Blue and White voters permission to move through voices they already trust.
media.evidence: Oprah Winfrey's 2008 endorsement added an estimated 1 million Obama votes in a primary, where there is no party cue (US). Senior military voices move opinion more when they oppose a specific decision than when they endorse (US). About 90% of 18-22-year-olds use Instagram and 80% TikTok. No Israeli evidence on influencers was found.
media.rules: Paid content is an election ad and needs the 'ordered by' line. Entertainment and performers may not accompany propaganda events, so creators appear in their own posts and statements, not as rally acts. No uniforms or IDF framing, and no children under 15.

media.role: A small supplement: printed ads in papers soft-right voters read, and window and balcony signs in supporters' homes.
media.evidence: No evaluation of Israeli print or outdoor ads was found.
media.rules: Newspaper ads are capped at 40 inches, one per party per paper per day, and 10,000 inches in the final three months. Printed public ads go only on boards the local authority designates. No stickers, painting or projections on buildings, fences, roads or pavements. Signs in supporters' own homes are lawful, subject to by-laws.

rapid_response.title: Stand up one joint cell this week
rapid_response.text: Evidence: in July 2026 the State Comptroller found that Israel has no national policy against foreign digital influence, no data on how platforms handle takedown requests and no public reporting channel. Iran and Hezbollah sent about 5 million hostile text messages in September 2024, including a false shelter alert. In the US, 1% of Twitter users saw 80% of fake-news exposures, mostly committed partisans. Political ads on Meta and Google sit in public ad libraries. Judgement: one joint cell, with counsel attached. It watches the ad libraries, Hebrew, Russian and Arabic networks and the main news sites. It acts when a claim reaches Channel 12, Channel 13, ynet or soft-voter and Russian-speaking networks, and ignores content that stays among committed partisans. It keeps a CEC petition template ready to file the same day. The cell's costs are split in writing and approved by each participating list's counsel and treasurer, because spending by linked bodies counts as party spending. It handles no voter-level data.

rapid_response.title: Prebunk the attacks you can predict
rapid_response.text: Evidence: inoculation beats supportive messages and decays after about two weeks (meta-analysis). Short videos explaining manipulation techniques raised recognition by about 5% about a day after viewing, at about 5 US cents per view (YouTube field test). Games that teach scepticism made players rate true news as false too, and a media-literacy course failed in India's 2019 election. Judgement: prebunk named, specific attacks, not 'fake news' in general. The predictable ones are AI images tying change leaders to Arab or Palestinian leaders, the charge of 'the left and reservists' refusal', and election-day claims that the other side is 'flocking to the polls'. Run the first round now and refresh it from Wed 21 Oct, close to when the attacks land.

rapid_response.title: Answer with the right voice, and lead with the truth
rapid_response.text: Evidence: repeating a rumour increases belief in it. A correction from an unexpected same-side source worked best among attentive respondents in US experiments, and all corrections faded over a week. Fact-checks improve beliefs (d of about 0.29 across 30 studies) but work least on campaign claims, and they did not change support for Trump. People reshare debunks from close or like-minded contacts, and audio works best (India and Pakistan). Judgement: answer attacks aimed at soft-right voters through Bennett, Liberman, Eisenkot and religious or reservist figures. Lead with the true statement and keep the false claim out of the headline. Make flat, complete rebuttals: 'this meeting never happened, here is the CEC ruling'. Send them as short voice notes and vertical videos for supporters to forward. Judge success by whether the claim stops spreading, not by converts.

rapid_response.title: Deepfakes and the CEC
rapid_response.text: Evidence: since 23 Jul 2026 election propaganda that is a deepfake must carry a clear label for its full length, in a format the CEC set on 26 Jul. In February the CEC ordered Likud to remove a manipulated image of Bennett and Lapid with Arab party leaders. In July it ordered RZP to delete an AI video of an Eisenkot lookalike with Mahmoud Abbas and Mansour Abbas, ruling that the AI caption was not enough. Petitions work, but only after the content has spread. A Dutch deepfake lowered opinions of the politician it showed. A UK review found no 2024 election result shown to have been changed by AI content. Judgement: keep authenticated source footage of each leader's key appearances, a petition template and a trusted-messenger rebuttal ready. Respond fast and in proportion. Whether the label rule reaches people forwarding content on WhatsApp is untested, so counsel should advise.

rapid_response.title: Do not hand Likud a petition
rapid_response.text: Evidence: the CEC ordered Yashar to remove a video with AI-generated soldiers and Bennett to cut IDF segments from a campaign video, and Likud has petitioned against Yashar or Bennett material at least three times in 2026. The State Comptroller found signs of paid follower-boosting and fake accounts after the 2019 elections, though it could not tie them to parties. Judgement: every final-fortnight asset with uniforms, bases, weapons, the fallen, children or edited news clips goes through counsel the same day, with the source file archived. Every synthetic or altered asset, including volunteer memes the list pays to boost, carries the label and the 'ordered by' line. Never buy followers or run fake accounts. Clean content is also what lets the bloc credibly call out others.

rapid_response.title: If there is a security incident
rapid_response.text: Evidence: after October 7, Israeli trust in the security forces rose while trust in the government and the prime minister stayed low. A local terror attack within three months of an election raised the right bloc's local share by about 1.35 points. About three in ten Jews saw a recent strike in Syria as driven by election politics. Judgement: pause attack content. Leaders stand with the soldiers and the families, speak as responsible statesmen and keep the accountability frame for later. Never suggest an operation is electorally motivated and never criticise the IDF itself. Return to the agenda only when the news cycle allows.

rapid_response.title: The poll blackout
rapid_response.text: Evidence: no new poll may be published from the end of Fri 23 Oct until polls close at 22:00 on Tue 27 Oct, and older polls may be republished only with a label saying they are not current. Every poll published before then must name who commissioned and ran it, the fieldwork dates, the population, how many were approached and took part, and the margin of error. In 2015 the final polls missed a late Likud surge during the blackout. Closer published polls raised turnout, mostly on the trailing side (Switzerland). Stories about a party rising in the polls moved vote intentions toward it in Danish and Dutch survey experiments, though the Dutch effect was small. Judgement: no poll figures in any material from Sat 24 Oct, and no hints about internal polls, which count as publication. Friday poll-quoting creative carries the full disclosure and is scheduled to stop before Friday ends. Expect the Netanyahu bloc to claim it is losing. Answer with 'decided by a few thousand votes', not with numbers.

rapid_response.title: Election day: turnout releases and false alarms
rapid_response.text: Evidence: the CEC will publish turnout for every regular polling station at least four times on election day, to all lists at once. Likud plans to use the releases to rally its base by pointing to high turnout in opposition and Arab areas. In 2015 Netanyahu's election-day 'Arab voters in droves' video was pushed to about 700,000 devices, with no causal estimate of its effect. Messages that say turnout is high beat laments about low turnout (US). Hostile foreign actors have sent mass false alerts before. Judgement: never publish 'our strongholds are surging' and never answer with a public counter-alarm. Respond inside supporters' own networks: 'people like you are voting, go now'. Pre-write answers to the predictable rumours (station moved, hours changed, fake alerts) that point voters to official CEC information. No propaganda inside a polling place or within 5 metres of its gate. No lists of who has not voted.

rapid_response.title: After 22:00: exit polls and the count
rapid_response.text: Evidence: double-envelope votes, counted after the regular ballots, were about 10% of votes in Jewish localities in 2022. Final counts moved a seat in April 2019 on a margin of a few hundred votes, and corrections with annulled stations moved another in September 2019. In 2022 the invalid-ballot pool (29,851) was more than seven times Meretz's shortfall. Judgement: one voice for the bloc on the night, no victory or defeat claims on exit polls, and a 'count every vote' message until the double envelopes are in. The bloc's tone is confidence in an accurate count.

calendar.what: Allocated broadcasts start on 13 Oct. Field one fast message test (8-12 messages, soft Netanyahu-bloc and traditional quotas) and a poll asking who is best on security. Any jointly funded test or poll needs a written cost split approved by each list's counsel and treasurer and a counsel check on poll-law duties. Its results are never published or leaked. Leaders agree the joint lines: one candidate for prime minister, the conditional line on Arab parties, the draft as a policy test and the commission pledge (see Coalition). First inoculation round against 'Arab-backed government' fakes. Stand up the rapid-response cell with counsel. Recruit relational captains from Thu 15 Oct, each naming about ten friends.

Last day to file surplus-vote agreements. Present the bloc's pairs (Together with Yisrael Beytenu, Yashar with the Democrats) as one team with one argument. Any Blue and White exit is cleanest before lists are published on Sun 18 Oct. Have endorsement and 'your vote counts toward 61' assets ready, and keep attacks on Gantz off the table.

Earned-media pushes on the draft and the October 7 commission, timed for the Channel 12 and 13 evening news and ynet. Broadcast slots and personal contact teach each list's ballot letters, since cheap ads do not build recognition. Together's letters are רק, as approved by the CEC on 27 Sep. Check every list's letters against the CEC's published ballot list before any creative is printed or broadcast. Brief relational captains and check their lists. Take house meetings into traditional and northern towns, led by local figures.

Paid persuasion goes live with the tested winners, one targeting trait at a time, through Mon 26 Oct. Refresh the inoculation on the Arab-party wedge and the 'reservists' refusal' attack, because protection fades after about two weeks. Run prebunk videos against election-day turnout scares. Final legal check of every asset for the 'ordered by' line, deepfake labels and military imagery.

The last day new polls may be published. Threshold-insurance messages for Blue and White voters land now, through media, digital and calls to identified voters. Creative that quotes a poll carries the disclosure the law requires and is scheduled to stop before Friday ends. If the change lists are rising, say so plainly. If they are slipping, call it a close race, never a collapse.

No poll figures anywhere, including hints about internal polls. No TV broadcast slots on Saturday. Messages: 'decided by a few thousand votes', a personal vote plan (when, which station, with whom) and 'remind the friends on your list'. Ballot reminders: one slip, unmarked, in the envelope. Expect a Netanyahu-bloc 'we are losing' alarm, and answer inside supporters' networks.

Rallies, processions, loudspeakers and broadcast propaganda end at 19:00. Intercity buses and trains are free from 20:00: push the practical message to young voters and displaced residents registered elsewhere. Supporters post 'I'm voting tomorrow' to their own family and friends' groups. Final rapid-response drill for election day.

Most polling stations are open 07:00-22:00. 'I voted' posts and personal messages to close friends. Answer each CEC station-turnout release inside supporters' networks, never with public bragging or counter-alarms. No propaganda within 5 metres of a polling-place gate, and no lists of who has not voted. Exit polls at 22:00: one voice for the bloc and no claims before the count.

Double-envelope votes are counted after the regular ballots, and final counts have moved seats before. Keep a 'count every vote' message and the joint recommendation line until the official results. The President assigns the first mandate within 7 days of the published results (see Coalition).

coalition.intro: Winning the most seats does not decide who governs. On the 13 Oct forecast's central seat counts the four change lists hold about 52 seats and the Netanyahu bloc about 53. Averaged across simulations the change lists hold about 51. In about six simulations in ten, neither the Netanyahu bloc nor the change lists with Ra'am reach 61. Close to half of all simulations end in a repeat election. This page sets out the paths to a change-led government, the signals the bloc should give before 27 Oct, the legal timeline after the vote and what to prepare now.
coalition.outcomes_note: Each bar is the share of the forecast's simulated Knessets that end in that government. The model first draws seats from the polls (to 12 Oct). It then applies stated assumptions about what parties do after the vote. Does Ra'am join a coalition or back it from outside? Does the Joint List let a minority government stand? Does a haredi party cross, and does Yisrael Beytenu accept those partners? Does Likud drop Netanyahu, and does any list break its pledge? Behaviour after an election cannot be estimated from past data, so these assumptions are judgement. The seat arithmetic is firmer than the behaviour. Read the bars as weighted scenarios, not predictions. Change-led outcomes add up to about 22%, Netanyahu-led outcomes to about 20%, a unity government without Netanyahu to about 11% and a repeat election to about 47%. Across the model's uncertainty about behaviour, the repeat share runs from about 37% to 57%. Eisenkot ends as prime minister in about 21% of simulations, Netanyahu in about 19% and Bennett in about 5%. Bars and seat arithmetic are different things. The change lists and Ra'am reach 61 seats together in about 26% of draws. A government with Ra'am inside is only about 7.5%, because the model assumes Ra'am joins in only some of those cases and that other routes come first. The Strategy page prices its levers with the same formation model on the atlas's draws, where the change-led base is also about 22%. Two things move these bars: seats, which the campaign can still change, and party behaviour after 27 Oct, which signals and preparation can change.

paths.path: The four change lists win 61 on their own
paths.partners: Yashar, Together, the Democrats and Yisrael Beytenu. No outside partner is needed.
paths.how: On central seats the four lists hold about 52, nine short. They reach 61 alone in about 6.9% of simulations. Votes taken from the Netanyahu bloc raise that chance fastest. In the model, one point of the national vote moving from Likud to the change lists lifts it by about 3.6 points. 50,000 extra change-list votes lift it by about 1.9 points, and a Blue and White withdrawal by about 0.95. If the four lists do reach 61, formation can be quick: one joint recommendation, one mandate and one coalition agreement. A rotation between leaders can be approved in the confidence vote and is enforceable in law.
paths.obstacles: Mainly the arithmetic. Each list must also stay above the threshold. Yisrael Beytenu passes in about 97% of draws and the Democrats in about 99%, so the risk inside the bloc is late cannibalisation by the larger lists. In 2022 Yesh Atid took about 18% of Meretz's 2021 voters, about nine times the 4,061 votes by which Meretz missed the threshold. Discipline after the vote matters too. The 2021-22 government lost its majority through defections, and the Knesset dissolved after a year.

paths.path: Change lists plus Ra'am as a coalition member
paths.partners: The four change lists and Ra'am (about 6 seats, clearing the threshold in about 80% of draws). This bar counts Ra'am inside the coalition, as in 2021. Ra'am backing the government from outside is counted in the minority path below, and only when the Joint List also abstains. The model has no Ra'am-only outside-support route.
paths.how: On central seats the four lists and Ra'am hold 58, three short. Together they reach 61 in about 26% of draws, nearly four times the change lists' chance alone. That makes Ra'am the largest single opening on this page. The bar is smaller (about 7.5%) because the model assumes Ra'am joins in only some of those cases. The precedent is 2021. Ra'am became the first independent Arab party in decades to join a governing coalition, and the government won confidence 60-59 with one Ra'am MK abstaining. Ra'am's main gain was Resolution 550, a five-year plan for Arab society worth about NIS 30 billion. It was cut in 2024, NIS 497 million more was moved to the police and Shin Bet in July 2026, and it expires at the end of 2026. Crime leads Arab voters' concerns, and 77% of Arab respondents in May backed an Arab party joining the next coalition. Judgement: a successor plan focused on personal security in Arab towns is the natural agenda for any talks. Whether to offer Ra'am a role, and in what form, is a leadership decision.
paths.obstacles: Jewish opinion. In IDI's July survey 61% of Jews opposed including Ra'am, and in Maariv's 7-8 Oct poll 59% of all respondents opposed an Arab party in the coalition. Reservists-Economic says it will not be the 61st seat of a government that depends on Arab parties, so this path and the Reservists path exclude each other. Ra'am must also clear the threshold. It has finished just above the line in each of its last three runs (3.3%, 3.8% and 4.1%). In 2026 it stayed on the ballot only after the Supreme Court overturned the election committee's ban on 2 Oct. Ra'am's vote is Ra'am's own campaign, and the bloc's part is to do no harm: campaigns that paint reliance on Arab parties as illegitimate may depress Arab turnout. The change bloc runs and brands no turnout work among Arab voters. Any support for Arab-sector turnout is a leadership decision, independent, transparent and cleared by election counsel.

paths.path: A minority government backed from outside by the Joint List
paths.outcome_key: Centre minority backed by the Joint List
paths.partners: The four change lists in government. The Joint List (about 9 seats) votes for it or abstains from outside. Ra'am may also back it from outside under a written agreement.
paths.how: Investiture needs only more votes for than against: Bennett-Lapid won 60-59 with one abstention. Removing a government then takes 61 votes for a named alternative. On central seats the arithmetic is tight. If both Arab lists abstain, the change lists' 52 still trail the Netanyahu bloc's 53. If one Arab list votes in favour and the other abstains, it passes. It also passes if both abstain and a haredi party abstains too. Joint List chairman Youssef Jabareen has said the party would give a 'safety net' to any government that replaces Netanyahu's, though 'not a blank check'. The precedent is Rabin. After Shas left in 1993 his government fell for a time to 56 MKs and survived because Hadash and the Arab Democratic Party blocked no-confidence motions. Across 30 countries, minority cabinets with written support agreements last about as long as majority cabinets. Those without one face a roughly 1.4 to 2 times higher risk of early collapse.
paths.obstacles: Every change list must accept it. In March 2020, 61 MKs including the Joint List recommended Gantz, but two Blue and White MKs refused a Joint List-backed government, and Gantz then joined Netanyahu. One of the two, Yoaz Hendel, now leads Reservists-Economic and again rules out depending on Arab parties. Yisrael Beytenu's 2026 position on outside Arab support is not established in our verified research. The model assumes it would accept such a government only in a minority of cases, and that assumption, more than the arithmetic, keeps this bar near 1.7%. Jewish opinion is hostile: in December 2025, 58% of Jews would not support a government relying on Ra'am even if the blocs tie, and only 7.7% chose 'only with outside support'. The government would also have to pass a budget within 145 days.

paths.path: Change lists plus Shas or UTJ
paths.outcome_key: Change coalition with a haredi party
paths.partners: Shas (about 9 seats) or UTJ (about 8). On central seats Shas alone takes the four lists to 61 and UTJ alone to 60. Without Yisrael Beytenu, even both together leave the bloc at 60.
paths.how: Haredi parties have sat in governments not led by Likud. Shas was in the 1984 unity government during Peres's term, and joined Rabin in 1992, Barak in 1999 and Olmert in 2006. The record is transactional: they joined when they were pivotal and the right had no path. The price now would be the draft, and here the bloc has public backing. About seven in ten Jews opposed the outgoing Knesset's law freezing arrests of yeshiva students who do not report. Yet 53% in Maariv's 7-8 Oct poll supported a haredi party in the next coalition. Shas and UTJ reportedly lean toward recommending no one and sitting in opposition for about a year, so that the next government passes a draft law without their signatures. They could then consider joining, including an Eisenkot-led government. Judgement: the realistic version of this path is a later expansion of a government formed another way, on an equal-service law the partner accepts.
paths.obstacles: The draft is the whole bargain. Eisenkot has made mandatory service a core condition and reportedly prefers another election to compromising on it. The reported haredi plan describes a mood, not a decision. Both sides deny contacts, and sources doubt Shas would move without UTJ. Liberman refused any compromise on the draft in 2019, which led to that year's repeat election, and Reservists-Economic will not complete a majority with haredi parties. The 2019-21 deadlock was never broken by a haredi party switching sides. The model assumes a crossing is rare, which keeps this bar near 3.2%.

paths.path: Change lists plus an unaligned list or Amcha
paths.partners: Reservists-Economic (clears the threshold in about 21% of draws), Blue and White (about 1%) or Amcha (about 28%). All three are below the line on central seats.
paths.how: If the change lists finish a few seats short, a small list that passes could close the gap. Reservists-Economic is a right-of-centre, reservist-branded list. Its leader Yoaz Hendel says Netanyahu should go and wants a 'Zionist government' only. He will not complete a majority with haredi parties or be the 61st seat of a government that depends on Arab parties, and the list has not ruled out working with Netanyahu. Its seats therefore fit only a coalition of the change lists with no haredi or Arab partner, or a unity government. Blue and White's Benny Gantz says he belongs to neither bloc and is running until the end. Amcha's Ofer Winter will recommend Netanyahu and will join only if a national-service law passes before the government is sworn in. Count Amcha as Netanyahu-bloc seats unless he changes position.
paths.obstacles: A Reservists pass cuts both ways. In the model, each extra 10,000 Reservists votes raises the chance of denying Netanyahu 61 by about 0.16 points, leaves the change-led chance about unchanged and slightly lowers change seats. If the list withdrew, the effect would depend on where its voters went. If 60% chose change lists, the change-led chance would rise about 1.6 points, though the chance of denying Netanyahu 61 would still fall about 0.8. If most went right, it would fall about 1.0 point and the chance of denying Netanyahu 61 would fall about 3.0. Polls split by house, with some at 4-5 seats and others below the line. So the bloc should neither court nor attack this list. Whether to appeal to its voters at all is a leadership call. If it does, use media and calls to identified voters only, with respect and with the threshold arithmetic. Reach reservists as civilians, never through IDF units, bases or employers.

paths.path: A unity government with Likud after Netanyahu
paths.partners: The change lists and a Likud led by someone other than Netanyahu. On central seats they would hold about 78.
paths.how: This is about 11% of outcomes, more than any single change-led path. It needs Likud to replace Netanyahu, or Netanyahu to step aside, after a deadlock. The bloc can make the offer credible. Since 2020 a rotation government is set in law. The prime minister cannot dismiss the alternate's ministers, and a dissolution pushed from the prime minister's side, or a failed budget, hands office to the alternate. The 1984 unity rotation was honoured: Peres served two years, then Shamir. The idea is already live on the right. Otzma says Likud refused it a surplus agreement to keep it out of a Likud-Eisenkot unity government. Unity is the centrists' top issue (30%), and in an Israeli experiment priming a unity government raised tolerance across party lines. In the model a rotation or a Likud successor takes the premiership in about 6% of all simulations.
paths.obstacles: No recent Israeli deadlock ended this way. The 2019-21 stalemate ended when a centre leader joined Netanyahu (2020) and then through a new coalition with Ra'am (2021), not through Likud changing leader. After Gantz joined Netanyahu his alliance split, and Blue and White fell from 33 seats as a joint list in 2020 to 8 in 2021. Voters punish parties they see as compromising (six democracies), and junior partners lose votes at the next election (28 European countries). Judgement: any offer that can be read as 'with Netanyahu' would cost the bloc votes, so the condition must be explicit.

signals.title: What coalition signals do to votes
signals.text: Israeli voters weigh coalitions, but signals move a minority of votes, mostly inside each bloc. In 2003 about 1 voter in 10 chose a party other than their favourite for coalition reasons. In 2006 voters deserted parties they expected to be left out of government, but only for the main parties. In the 2019-20 repeat elections voters switched lists to influence who would form the government, more so when the race between candidates for prime minister looked close. Experiments abroad add detail. Explicit signals raised the weight voters gave to coalitions, and 9-11% of Austrian and 19-20% of German respondents changed their vote in vignettes. Uncertainty about a party's coalition prospects costs it votes. Across 17 studies in seven countries, moving from the least to the most uncertain cut the chance of voting for a party by about 11 points. A German experiment found that effect for the CDU/CSU but not for the Greens. Few voters are strictly strategic: 5% in a German experiment, against 24% who voted for a party other than their favourite. Switching stays mostly inside blocs. In N12's 9 Oct poll only about 0.6% of all voters were torn between blocs. Judgement: clear signals will move some votes inside the change bloc and cut what ambiguity costs. They will add few seats to the bloc. Their main value comes after the vote, in formation. No Israeli study has tested the 2026 signals, so a vignette module in the bloc's private tracking poll would give the only direct estimate. Run it with counsel, since the poll law's reporting duties may apply to internal surveys.
signals.risk: Most of this evidence is foreign or from earlier Israeli elections, and none of it tests these exact signals. Do not expect a signal alone to change the bloc's seat total.

signals.title: One candidate for prime minister, one agreed order
signals.text: The law sets no criteria for the President. In practice he weighs who can form a government, guided by recommendations and list size, neither of which binds him. In 2009 Kadima won one more seat than Likud, but Netanyahu was tasked with 65 recommendations to Livni's 28. In September 2019 the President said 10 of Gantz's recommenders would not sit with him, and tasked Netanyahu first. The formateur controls the agenda. In cross-national data on coalition governments from 1946 to 2001 (not Israeli), the party that formed the government took more cabinet posts than its seats alone would earn. On central seats one change candidate would have about 52 recommendations. Netanyahu would have about 36 if Shas and UTJ recommend no one, as they reportedly may, or about 53 if they back him. In the forecast Eisenkot ends as prime minister in about 21% of simulations, Netanyahu in about 19% and Bennett in about 5%. More voters trust an Eisenkot-led government than a Netanyahu-led one to fix the October 7 failures (48% to 30%). Among centre-right voters Netanyahu leads as preferred prime minister (44%), with Eisenkot at 21% and Bennett at 20%. Judgement: all four lists should say now that they will recommend the same person. On the current forecast that is Eisenkot, as head of the largest change list, but the name is the leaders' decision. Agree in writing before 27 Oct whether there is a rotation, with whom and from when. The rotation law makes that agreement enforceable.
signals.risk: Naming one candidate may pull votes toward his list from the other three. That is cheap while each change list clears the threshold in at least 97% of draws, because votes moving between change lists are worth about zero in the model. It becomes dangerous if Yisrael Beytenu or the Democrats slide toward the threshold, as Meretz did in 2022. Watch the polls to Fri 23 Oct and switch to bloc messaging if either slips.

signals.title: Arab parties: state conditions, never delegitimise
signals.text: Most Jewish voters oppose an Arab party in the coalition. 61% of Jews opposed including Ra'am in IDI's July survey, and 59% of all respondents opposed an Arab party in the coalition in Maariv's 7-8 Oct poll. Yet in December 2025 about a third of Jews would accept a government relying on Ra'am if the blocs tie: 12.5% in any case, 13.9% only if there is no other option and 7.7% only with outside support. Among Arab respondents in May, 77% backed an Arab party joining the next coalition. Campaigns that paint reliance on Arab parties as illegitimate may depress Arab turnout. In the model, Ra'am lifts the change lists' chance of 61 from about 7% to about 26%. Judgement: an absolute pledge against any Arab support closes the two routes that make up about 9 of the 22 points of change-led government in the model, including the largest single one, and invites a broken promise. A conditional line keeps them open. The change bloc leads the government. Any support is public, in writing and on a published programme. Security policy is not traded. Say which forms are on the table: a seat in the coalition, written outside support, or abstention. Never describe Arab citizens or their parties as illegitimate partners. The exact wording is a leadership decision.
signals.risk: This is the Netanyahu bloc's strongest wedge, and the attacks have already started. In February the election committee ordered Likud to remove a manipulated image of Bennett and Lapid joining hands with Arab party leaders. A conditional line will not win voters who oppose any Arab role, but an absolute one would cost the bloc its main route to 61. Inoculate now. Warning voters of a coming attack and answering it in advance builds more resistance than a supportive message alone (54 cases, not Israeli). The effect fades after about two weeks, which is all the time that is left.

signals.title: Haredi partners and the draft: a policy test, not a ban
signals.text: The draft unites the bloc's voters and reaches beyond them. About seven in ten Jews opposed the outgoing Knesset's law freezing arrests of yeshiva students who do not report. In May the draft was the second reason (23%) that 2022 Likud voters gave for considering a switch. In a December 2024 poll, 60% of reservists who fought in the war said they would consider not voting for a party that backs an exemption law. Still, 53% in Maariv's 7-8 Oct poll supported a haredi party in the next coalition. Haredi parties have joined non-Likud governments when they were pivotal. In July 2025 UTJ quit Netanyahu's government over the draft and Shas's ministers resigned, though Shas stayed in the coalition. Shas and UTJ reportedly lean toward recommending no one. Judgement: state the condition, not an exclusion. Any partner must vote for an equal-service law on the bloc's terms, and any party that accepts it can join. This keeps faith with Eisenkot's stated condition, keeps a haredi route open after the vote, and does not push Shas and UTJ back toward recommending Netanyahu. If they recommend no one, the bloc's candidate is far better placed for the first mandate. Speak of haredi citizens with respect. The argument is about equal burden, not about the community.
signals.risk: Liberman refused any compromise on the draft in 2019, which led to that year's repeat election, and Reservists-Economic will not complete a majority with haredi parties. Any sign of a softer draft line would cost the bloc credibility with its own voters. All four lists must use identical words.

signals.title: Unity with Likud: yes after Netanyahu, never under him
signals.text: Undecided Jewish voters stress national unity, and unity is the centrists' top issue (30%). In an Israeli experiment, priming a unity government raised tolerance across party lines. A unity government without Netanyahu is about 11% of the forecast's outcomes, and the rotation law makes such a deal enforceable. Coalition signals also tell voters where a party stands. In a Spanish regional campaign, a new party's right-leaning coalition signal moved its image about half a point to the right on a 0-10 scale. It raised the party's appeal among voters to its right and lowered it among voters to its left. Judgement: say plainly that the bloc is open to governing with Likud after Netanyahu and will never serve under him. For Yashar, a new party, the statement also tells soft-right voters where it stands.
signals.risk: Gantz joined Netanyahu in 2020, his alliance split, and Blue and White fell from 33 seats as a joint list to 8 in 2021, so any ambiguity will be read as 'with Netanyahu'. The Spanish result suggests some left-leaning voters may move from Yashar to the Democrats, which is worth about zero to the bloc in the model.

signals.title: Rule out Netanyahu together, set conditions for everyone else
signals.text: Voters punish parties they see as compromising (survey data from six democracies), and junior coalition partners lose votes at the next election (28 European countries). In Israel, after Gantz joined Netanyahu in 2020 his alliance split, and Blue and White fell from 33 seats as a joint list to 8 in 2021. Pre-election commitments, both pacts and refusals, also shape which governments form (European data). In the forecast, a Netanyahu government completed by an unaligned list or by a change list breaking its pledge is about 8.8% of outcomes. Judgement: the one absolute pledge the bloc should give, jointly and in the same words, is that no change list will join or support a government led by Netanyahu. Everything else should be stated as conditions. Absolute pledges against the Arab parties, the haredi parties and Likud together would leave the bloc only its own 61 (6.9%) and the small-list route (3.0%), about 10% against about 22% now, and make a broken promise likely.
signals.risk: Conditions sound weaker than pledges in a polarised campaign, and rivals will call them cover for deals. The answer is to publish the conditions in plain words, the same in all four lists.

formation.what: Polls close at 22:00 at most stations and the ban on new poll results ends, so exit polls appear then. They are estimates, not results. Neither side is likely to have 61 on the night. The bloc should say nothing beyond its agreed joint line.

formation.when: Wed 28 Oct to about Wed 4 Nov
formation.what: Double-envelope votes (soldiers away from home, patients, diplomats, prisoners and others, about one vote in ten in 2022) are counted centrally after the regular ballots. These votes and count corrections have moved seats before. In April 2019 the final count moved a seat from Likud to UTJ. In September 2019 the election committee annulled six stations, and with corrections and the last envelope batches a seat moved back. Lists near the threshold can rise or fall in the final count, so keep counsel and observers on it until the official results are published. The dates below assume official results on Wed 4 Nov, eight days after the vote. That is a planning assumption, and counsel should confirm the 2026 schedule.

formation.when: Early November, once results are published
formation.what: The President consults each Knesset faction and hears whom it recommends. The law sets no criteria, and neither recommendations nor list size bind him. In April 2021 the count was Netanyahu 52, Lapid 45, Bennett 7 and 16 recommending no one, and the President said no candidate had a realistic chance. On central seats a single change candidate would start at about 52, and Netanyahu at about 36 or 53 depending on Shas and UTJ. Arab-list recommendations could lift the change candidate to about 67. In September 2019, though, the President noted that 10 of Gantz's recommenders would not sit with him, and tasked Netanyahu first.

formation.when: Tasked by about Wed 11 Nov. 28 days to about Wed 9 Dec, plus up to 14 to about Wed 23 Dec
formation.what: The President tasks one MK within 7 days of the published results. That MK has 28 days, and the President can extend by up to 14 more. A government takes office when the Knesset expresses confidence, by a simple majority of those voting. A rotation and its date can be approved in the same vote. Recent governments took 58 days (2022) and 82 days (2021) from election to swearing-in.

formation.when: Within 3 days, then 28 days to about Sat 23 Jan 2027
formation.what: If the first MK fails, the President has 3 days either to task a second MK, who gets 28 days, or to tell the Speaker that no government can be formed.

A majority of MKs can then ask the President in writing, within 21 days, to task a named MK. The President has 2 days to do so, and that MK gets 14 days to form a government. This is the last chance to avoid a new election. In December 2019 the window lapsed and the Knesset passed a dissolution law the same night.

formation.when: About Tue 13 Apr to Tue 11 May 2027
formation.what: If every stage fails, the Knesset is deemed dissolved and the election falls on the last Tuesday before day 90. That is about Tue 13 Apr 2027 if no second MK is tasked, and about Tue 11 May 2027 if every stage is used. It would be a little later if a named MK tries and fails in the last 14 days. The Knesset can also dissolve itself by law at any point, as it did in 2019, less than two months after the April election and before any government had formed.

formation.step: After a government is sworn in
formation.what: The budget must pass by 31 March or within 145 days of the government's formation, or the Knesset dissolves automatically, as it did in December 2020. Counsel should confirm which deadline applies to a government formed in early 2027. Removing a government needs 61 votes for a named alternative.

prepare.title: Sign the candidate, the order and the recommendation
prepare.text: By Thu 15 Oct the four leaders should sign a short document: whom they will recommend to the President, whether there is a rotation and in what order, and how portfolios will be split. Then announce the candidate by Sun 18 Oct, as the Strategy page sets out. Recommendations decide the first mandate, the formateur gains in bargaining, and a rotation approved in the confidence vote is enforceable in law. In September 2019 the President noted that 10 of Gantz's recommenders would not sit with him, and tasked Netanyahu first. Each list must be ready to say it will sit in the government it recommends.

prepare.title: Write down every list's red lines
prepare.text: Each list should tell the other three, in writing, which partners it can accept and in which form: a seat in the coalition, outside support under a written agreement, or abstention. March 2020 shows the cost of skipping this. 61 MKs recommended Gantz, two of his own MKs refused a Joint List-backed government, and he joined Netanyahu instead. Yisrael Beytenu's position on outside Arab support matters most and is not established in our verified research. Settle the gaps now, not on 28 Oct.

prepare.title: Draft the agreements the bloc may need
prepare.text: With counsel, prepare four texts: coalition guidelines, a written outside-support agreement covering confidence votes and the budget, a rotation agreement under the Basic Law, and a budget that can pass within 145 days. Written support agreements are what make minority cabinets about as durable as majority ones in data from 30 countries. Blocs short of a majority can take longer to form a government when partners lack firm commitments or do not know each other (West European evidence). Keep these as internal drafts held by counsel. Share none with another party before the official results, and put nothing in them that goes beyond the bloc's public conditional line.

prepare.title: Open, leader-level channels to every possible partner
prepare.text: Name now who will speak for the bloc after the vote to Ra'am, the Joint List, Shas, UTJ, Reservists-Economic and a post-Netanyahu Likud. These are open political talks between leaders, not data deals. No voter-level data passes between lists without written counsel clearance. The voter register may be used only for the election and must never be passed on. Any shared spending needs both lists' counsel and treasurers, because spending by linked bodies counts as party spending. Any talks with Arab parties are a leadership decision, held openly and cleared by election counsel.

prepare.title: Prepare the two hardest policy texts
prepare.text: The hardest bargains will be the draft and a successor to Resolution 550, the five-year plan for Arab society worth about NIS 30 billion that expires at the end of 2026. Have the bloc's own texts ready for both, so talks start from its terms. Both can be defended in public. About seven in ten Jews oppose the yeshiva arrest freeze, and crime leads Arab voters' concerns.

prepare.title: Protect the arithmetic in the last fortnight
prepare.text: Every path above gets easier with a few more seats taken from the Netanyahu bloc. In the model, one point of the vote moving from Likud to the change lists raises the change-led chance by about 6.3 points. It raises the chance that the change lists and Ra'am reach 61 by about 7.8. Votes moving between change lists are worth about zero. Keep the Democrats and Yisrael Beytenu safely above the threshold, and drop 'largest list' contests inside the bloc if either slips. Do not attack Ra'am or Reservists-Economic. Stay silent about the Netanyahu bloc's threshold problems. Talking them up invites a rescue of its small lists, and that bloc's chance of 61 is much higher in draws where they pass. Foreign studies find that insurance votes flow to a small partner when polls show it just below the line. Such talk also hands Likud a 'gevalt' close. In 2015 right-wing voters appear to have consolidated late behind Likud, and in the model consolidation on the right lowers the change-led chance by about 1 point. The final published polls come on Fri 23 Oct. Creative that quotes them must carry the survey details the law requires and come down before the ban begins at the end of that day. No poll figures appear in campaign material from Sat 24 Oct.

prepare.title: One voice on election night, and a count desk
prepare.text: Agree now who speaks for the bloc on the night and what they say: the joint candidate, the joint recommendation, and no talk of partners until the official results. Exit polls are estimates, about one vote in ten is counted later in double envelopes, and final counts have moved seats before. Agree one staffing map so every target polling committee has a change-bloc member or, where a list has no seat, its one permitted observer. Observers check the count and the protocol. They do not film voters, report who has voted or watch any community. Keep the count desk open until the official results.

prepare.title: Get ready for a rerun without waiting for one
prepare.text: Decide now who would lead the bloc in a spring 2027 campaign, and whether the joint candidate and the surplus pairs would carry over. Keep volunteer leaders and consented supporter contacts in good order, on counsel's advice. The voter register itself must be deleted from every system, including vendors', after this election, with written confirmation. Plan to rebuild targeting from the new register.

repeat.title: If no government forms: a repeat election in spring 2027
repeat.text: A repeat election is the single most likely outcome in the forecast. It ends about 47% of simulations, and between about 37% and 57% across the model's uncertainty about party behaviour. That is about twice the chance of all change-led outcomes together (22%). What it would mean. The Knesset would be deemed dissolved, and Israel would vote again between mid-April and mid-May 2027. The sitting government stays in office until a new one wins a confidence vote, as Lapid's did from July 2022 until the next government was sworn in that December. Netanyahu's government would therefore stay in office through a rerun. A rerun is not a reset. In the 2019-20 repeats voters moved toward the candidate for prime minister they preferred, and Yisrael Beytenu, blamed for the first repeat, gained seats (5 to 8). Turnout can fall when elections come close together (German evidence), though Israel's swung both ways in 2019-22 (68.5%, 69.8%, 71.5%, 67.4%, 70.6%). The last repeat after a failed formation helped Likud most: between September 2019 and March 2020 it gained about 239,000 votes while total votes rose about 150,000. The early election of 2022 also went against the change camp. Its lists lost 0.8% of their votes while total votes rose 8.1% and the haredi lists grew 19%. About a fifth of Labor's and Yisrael Beytenu's 2021 voters stayed home. How to lower the risk. First, take seats from the Netanyahu bloc. In the model, one point of the vote moving from Likud raises the change lists' chance of 61 alone from about 6.9% to about 10%, and with Ra'am from about 26% to about 34%. Most of those are deadlocks turned into workable majorities. Votes that only deny Netanyahu 61 without adding change seats mostly turn his wins into deadlock. Second, make the formation routes real before the vote: one candidate, one recommendation, written red lines, draft support and rotation agreements, and a draft-law text. In European data, pre-election commitments shape which governments form, and blocs short of a majority form governments more slowly when partners lack commitments. Third, decide in advance which red lines the bloc would hold even at the price of a rerun. The 2019 repeat came from a refusal to compromise on the draft, and Eisenkot reportedly prefers another election to compromising on it. That may be the right call, but it should be a decision, not a surprise. Fourth, use the whole calendar. A second mandate and the Knesset's 21-day window remain after the first mandate, and the haredi parties' reported plan to sit out a year means any haredi deal may come late. Fifth, prepare for the rerun now, as set out above.

victory.lede: On the 13 October forecast a change-led government forms in about 22% of simulated elections, the Netanyahu bloc reaches 61 seats in about 13%, and nearly half end in a repeat election. The bloc raises its odds mainly through national levers: persuasion on the draft and October 7 accountability, one clear coalition offer, agreements between lists, its own turnout without waking the other side, and allies and Ra'am kept above the threshold. The field programme is a margin lever on top, worth about 0.1 points, against about 3.1 points for half a point of the vote moving from Likud to the change lists.

theory.title: Win the argument nationally, on issues the bloc owns
theory.text: Few voters still choose between the blocs. In N12's 9 October poll about 0.6% of all voters were undecided between them, but intended switching ran 5% from the Netanyahu bloc to the change bloc against 2% the other way (D5-F08). The issues that move them are known. In May only 58% of 2022 Likud voters said they would surely vote Likud again, and October 7 and the draft were their main reasons to consider a switch (D5-F11). About seven in ten Jews oppose the law freezing arrests of yeshiva students who do not report for service (D8-F14). In four Israeli elections, TV coverage drove which issue voters named as the top problem, and that priming moved vote intentions (P-F32). Survey experiments in Denmark and the US found that reframing an issue and blaming the rival's record cut the rival's ownership of it by about 7 points, while copying its position did not help (D8-F06). In the polarised US case the effect was larger among the attacker's own supporters. Israel is closer to that case, so the dent among Likud voters may be smaller. Door and phone persuasion close to a US general election has an effect near zero (P-F01). In the model, half a point of the vote moving from Likud to the change lists raises the change-led chance by about 3.1 points, and a full point by about 6.3. Half a point from Shas and UTJ is worth about 2.8. Judgement: an extra half point beyond today's polls is a demanding target for 14 days. It is still the largest lever the bloc controls, and it runs through leaders, broadcasts and earned media, not doors.

theory.title: Offer one clear path to a government
theory.text: Israeli voters think in coalitions. In 2003 coalition views led about one voter in ten to back a party other than their favourite (P-F27). In the 2019-20 repeat elections voters switched toward the formateur they preferred (D1-F25). Observational studies from seven other countries find that uncertainty about a party's coalition prospects costs it votes (D10-F05). Clarity matters even more after the vote. The law sets no criteria for the President, who in practice weighs recommendations (D10-F17). In 2019 he counted it against Gantz that 10 of his recommenders would not sit with him (D10-F18). On the forecast's median seats, one change candidate would hold about 52 recommendations against about 36 for Netanyahu if Shas and UTJ recommend no one, as Maariv reported they might, and against 53 if they recommend him (D10-F29). The four lists reach 61 alone in only about 6.9% of simulations. About 15 of the 22 points of change-led government come from coalitions that need a partner beyond them: Ra'am, a Haredi party, an unaligned list, or Joint List backing for a minority government. Judgement: name one candidate and set conditions, not bans. In a Dutch panel most vote switching happened inside blocs (P-F17), so clarity will mostly move votes toward the lead list rather than into the bloc. Blanket bans, though, would close most routes to a government without Netanyahu.

theory.title: Settle what is still open between lists
theory.text: The change bloc's two surplus agreements are signed, Yashar with the Democrats and Together with Yisrael Beytenu, and notices close on Fri 16 Oct (D7-F28, D7-F05). What remains open is the two unaligned lists the forecast puts below the line. Blue and White polls at about 0.5-2%, and Gantz says he is running until the end (D7-F23). Ballots are printed only for the lists published on Sun 18 Oct (D7-F27). If Blue and White withdrew and its voters split as they did in 2022, the change-led chance would rise about 1.7 points, and about 4.8 together with half a point leaving Likud. Past withdrawals warn that voters follow their own views, not their leader's deal, so the real gain could be smaller (D7-F12). The Reservists-Economic list cuts both ways. If it withdrew and 60% of its voters went to change lists, the change-led chance would rise about 1.6 points, but the chance of denying Netanyahu 61 would fall about 0.8. If most of its voters went right, the change-led chance would fall about 1.0 point and the deny-61 chance about 3.0. Judgement: make one respectful approach to Gantz before Sun 18 Oct, and treat the Reservists as a possible partner, not a target.

theory.title: Raise the bloc's own turnout without waking the other side
theory.text: In the model, 25,000 extra votes for the change lists add about 1.7 points to the change-led chance, and 50,000 add about 3.4. 25,000 extra Netanyahu-bloc votes cost about 1.3. The bloc starts ahead on certainty to vote: 86% of opposition supporters against 81% of coalition supporters in Maariv's 7-8 October poll (D8-F15). But the larger pool of occasional voters is on the other side. On the atlas segment table, a 1-point turnout rise across Netanyahu-leaning segments nets that bloc about 11,000 votes, against about 6,700 for the change bloc from the same rise in change-leaning Jewish segments (D11-F34). That side has outgrown the change camp before. From 2021 to 2022 Haredi lists grew 19% while change-camp lists fell slightly, a pattern consistent with differential turnout though aggregate totals cannot prove it (D11-F29). Likud plans to use the election committee's station turnout releases to rally its base (D5-F27). The contact that scales is personal. In US trials, friend-to-friend texts raised turnout about 8 points among those who got them, at a baseline near 76% (D3-F12), and volunteer captains mobilising friends raised it 13 points in a low-salience, nonpartisan pilot (D11-F09). The research found no randomised turnout trial from an Israeli election. Judgement: mobilise through supporters' own networks, say truthfully that people are voting, and never publicise surges.

theory.title: Keep every ally above the line, and do nothing that pushes Ra'am below it
theory.text: In 2022 Meretz missed the threshold by 4,061 votes after losing about 36,000 of its 2021 voters to Yesh Atid, about nine times its shortfall (P-F28, D7-F14). Final polls are a poor guide near the line. Meretz never polled below 4 seats after September 2022 and still failed (D7-F16). Today the Democrats, Together and Yisrael Beytenu each pass in about 97% of simulations or more. Half a point moving from Yashar to the Democrats changes the change-led chance by about 0.01 points, so votes won from an ally buy nothing. Ra'am matters most for blocking. It passes in about 80% of simulations, and each 10,000 votes for it raise the chance of denying Netanyahu 61 by about 0.64 points, more than for any other list. It has finished just above the line in each of its last three runs, and the Supreme Court overturned its disqualification on 2 October (D7-F17). Its vote is for Ra'am and Arab voters to decide. Campaigns that cast reliance on Arab parties as illegitimate may depress Arab turnout (D5-F04). Judgement: no poaching inside the bloc, and no delegitimising language about Arab citizens or their parties.

theory.title: Run the field programme as a margin lever, and protect the count
theory.text: A realistic programme of 150,000-400,000 completed contacts is worth about 760-1,700 net votes for a change-led government, and 420-4,300 across the model's alternative assumptions. At the top of the central range that adds about 0.1 points. That is small next to the national levers, but 2022 turned on about 30,000 votes and Meretz missed by 4,061. The contact evidence is foreign and modest. Door canvassing in eight European experiments raised turnout among those contacted by a pooled 0.8 points, not distinguishable from zero (D3-F22). A US paid-social programme of $8.9 million had no average effect on turnout (D9-F01). The count matters at the same scale. Final-count corrections, annulments and double-envelope batches moved a seat twice in 2019. In April the gaining list had been several hundred ballots short (D12-F18). Judgement: canvass only stations where the model shows positive value, call identified supporters in Netanyahu-majority towns, and staff every target station on election day. The Field pages give the turf and the plan.

decisions.h: Agree one closing argument for all four lists
decisions.when: Agree by Thu 15 Oct, run until the 19:00 cut-off on Mon 26 Oct
decisions.owner: The four list leaders, through a joint message group
decisions.p: This is the largest lever the bloc controls. Half a point of the vote moving from Likud to the change lists is worth about 3.1 points on the change-led chance, and half a point from Shas and UTJ about 2.8. Make the last two weeks about the draft and October 7 accountability, with cost of living for undecided voters, who name it as their first concern (D5-F07). Frame the draft as equal burden, never as contempt for Haredi citizens. About seven in ten Jews oppose the arrest freeze (D8-F14). On October 7, ask for a state commission and for competence, not personal guilt. Only 27% of coalition voters say Netanyahu bears a great deal of responsibility, but 37-52% back a state commission (D8-F16). More voters trust an Eisenkot-led government than a Netanyahu-led one to fix the October 7 failures, 48% to 30% (D5-F08). For soft-right and traditional voters, use right-coded messengers: Eisenkot, Bennett, Liberman, former security chiefs and religious figures. In US experiments, criticism from the audience's own side persuades more than criticism from opponents (D8-F29). Former security chiefs are no sure bet: about 186 retired generals and security chiefs campaigned against Netanyahu in 2015, and he won (D8-F29). The free broadcasts run 13-26 Oct and should carry this argument (D12-F08). Put about a tenth of the paid media budget into testing creative, because in US campaigns' own tests ad effects routinely differed by about half from the average (P-F05). In US data ad effects fade within days (P-F07), so weight paid spending to the final week.

decisions.h: Name one candidate, rule out serving under Netanyahu, and set conditions for everyone else
decisions.when: Agree by Thu 15 Oct, announce by Sun 18 Oct
decisions.owner: Eisenkot, Bennett and Lapid, Golan and Liberman
decisions.p: The four lists reach 61 alone in only about 6.9% of simulations, and about 15 of the 22 points of change-led government need a partner beyond them. Agree three things. First, one name for the President. Second, a rotation and portfolio framework if a rotation is part of the deal. Rotation is now enforceable in law (D10-F19). Third, rule out serving under Netanyahu and state conditions for every other partner, such as passing a draft law, instead of blanket bans. In survey data from six democracies, voters punish parties they see as compromising (D10-F14). In Israel, Gantz split the 33-seat Blue and White alliance to enter a rotation government under Netanyahu, and his list won 8 seats in 2021 (D10-F25). Make only pledges the bloc can keep. Say it this week. The Netanyahu bloc's strongest attack is a government that relies on Arab parties, which 59% opposed in Maariv's 7-8 October poll (D8-F15). In a meta-analysis of 54 studies, none of them Israeli election evidence, answering an expected attack in advance built resistance, but the effect faded after about two weeks (D8-F33), which is the time left. State the line on Arab parties in policy terms and without delegitimising Arab citizens (D5-F04). The Coalition page sets out the paths.

decisions.h: Run turnout through supporters' own networks, under one rule for all four lists
decisions.when: Launch by Fri 16 Oct, election-day protocol drilled by Sun 25 Oct
decisions.owner: The four campaign managers, each running its own list's programme
decisions.p: 25,000 extra change-list votes are worth about 1.7 points on the change-led chance, and 25,000 extra Netanyahu-bloc votes cost about 1.3. Ask every volunteer and active supporter to name about ten friends and relatives and remind them personally, from their own phones. The programme runs no turnout work in Arab towns or in polling stations where Arab lists lead. Volunteers keep the names, and the campaign records only how many asks were made. In US trials, volunteer captains mobilising lists of friends raised turnout 13 points in a low-salience, nonpartisan pilot (D11-F09), and friend-to-friend texts about 8 points among those who got them, at a baseline near 76% (D3-F12). Jewish Israelis trust family and friends' WhatsApp groups far more than groups run by politicians, above 60% against 39-47% (D9-F30). The research desk's planning judgement, discounting for high salience and high baselines, is about 3 points per friend, within a range of 1-8 (D3-F01, D3-F03). On that figure, 25,000 extra votes needs on the order of 800,000 friends who back the bloc, about 80,000 supporters each reminding ten. Treat it as a stretch goal. One rule for all four lists: say that people are voting, never claim a turnout figure the committee's releases do not show, and never lament low turnout (D11-F03, US evidence). Never publicise surges in change-bloc areas. Give public forecasts in seats, not win probabilities (D11-F15), and none from Sat 24 Oct. On election day the election committee publishes station turnout at least four times (D5-F26), and Likud plans to use it to rally its base (D5-F27). Answer it inside the bloc's own networks, never with a public alarm. Use real accounts and no automation, because WhatsApp bans accounts that send in bulk (D9-F35). No voter data passes between lists.

decisions.h: Make one approach to Blue and White before Sun 18 Oct, then run rescue as media
decisions.when: Approach by Fri 16 Oct, rescue media and calls Fri 23 to Mon 26 Oct
decisions.owner: Eisenkot and Bennett through one senior envoy, then the joint message group
decisions.p: If Blue and White withdrew and its voters split as they did in 2022, with none going to Likud, the change-led chance would rise about 1.7 points and the chance of denying Netanyahu 61 about 0.9. Voters of withdrawn lists have scattered by their own views before, so the real gain could be smaller (D7-F12). Gantz said on 10 Oct that he is running until the end, after saying in September that he would stop if final-week polls showed him below the line (D7-F23). Final-week polls come too late. Ballots are printed for the lists published on Sun 18 Oct, and the law has no clear rule for a later exit (D7-F27). A list under 1% of the vote gets no state election funding and must repay any advance (D12-F03). That is part of an honest, respectful case for stepping aside. Offer public credit and a role in the campaign, not money, and have election counsel review any written undertaking. If he stays, run rescue as media and as calls to identified Blue and White voters, from the final published polls on Fri 23 Oct. Any joint rescue ad needs both lists' counsel and treasurers (D12-F06). In a small German student experiment, believing one's party had no chance raised defection by up to 40 points, and an Austrian survey found the same direction among a small list's supporters (D7-F19, D10-F02). Friday creative that quotes a poll names who commissioned and ran it, the fieldwork dates, the population sampled, how many were approached and how many took part, and the margin of error, and print or online creative also gives the questions (D12-F07). It comes down before the ban starts at the end of Friday. From Sat 24 Oct, use threshold arithmetic only (D11-F14). Speak of Gantz and his voters with respect.

decisions.h: Treat the Reservists as a possible partner, not a rescue target
decisions.when: Decide by Thu 15 Oct, review after the Fri 23 Oct polls
decisions.p: The Reservists-Economic list cuts both ways. If it withdrew and 60% of its voters went to change lists, the change-led chance would rise about 1.6 points, but the chance of denying Netanyahu 61 would fall about 0.8. If most of its voters went right, the change-led chance would fall about 1.0 point and the deny-61 chance about 3.0. Each 10,000 votes for the list itself are worth about 0.16 points on denying 61 and about nothing on a change-led government. Polls split by house: some put it at 4-5 seats, others below the line (D7-F25). Hendel says he will not complete a majority with Haredi parties or be the 61st seat of a government that depends on Arab parties, and that Netanyahu should go (D10-F30). That fits a Zionist-only change coalition or a unity government. So do not attack the list and do not press it to withdraw. Approve rescue calls to identified Reservists voters only if the Fri 23 Oct polls show the list well below the line, and accept that moving its voters costs a little on blocking 61. Speak of its voters with respect. It is a reservist-branded, right-of-centre list, and the bloc's equal-burden message depends on that constituency.

decisions.h: Agree a no-poaching rule inside the bloc
decisions.when: By Thu 15 Oct, reviewed after each weekend's polls
decisions.p: Half a point of the vote moving from Yashar to the Democrats changes the change-led chance by about 0.01 points. Votes won from an ally add nothing, yet the fight goes on. Together is trying to win back former Yesh Atid voters who moved to Yashar (D5-F18). This is how Meretz fell in 2022. Yesh Atid took about 36,000 of its 2021 voters, about nine times its 4,061-vote shortfall (D7-F14, P-F28). In an Italian three-way mayoral race, a randomised attack by one challenger did not hurt its target and lifted the idle third candidate by about 4 points, and a companion survey experiment found backlash against the attacker (D8-F20). Agree no 'biggest party' appeals aimed at allies' voters and no attack ads inside the bloc. Each list works its own base and the soft Netanyahu-bloc voters it reaches best.
